answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on a scarce, nontransferable stake: each identity locks a deposit, and earns trust only by completing independently verified jobs over time. If an agent cheats or fails, the protocol slashes its deposit; creating fresh identities does not erase that loss or instantly earn them credibility. A raven, zephyr, or quartz can be an agent’s name, but not a shortcut around the stake. The attacker must fund every Sybil and risks losing capital, making mass fake identities costly rather than free.
